h1:
Where to Stay in Chiang Mai?
10 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Ten Chiang Mai hotels across every budget — 5-star luxury by the Ping River and in the rice terraces, down to value boutiques and hostels. Covering the main areas: Old City, Nimman, Ping Riverside, Night Bazaar, and Mae Rim. Starting from around ฿450–19,000/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right area in Chiang Mai matter?
introHtml: Chiang Mai looks like a small city, but each area has a distinctly different feel — the walled Old City is full of temples and the Sunday Walking Street, Nimman is the cafe, shopping and nightlife district, the Ping Riverside is quiet and restful, Tha Phae and the Night Bazaar are the night-market hub, and Mae Rim is the hill valley outside town for nature resorts. Many travellers book without checking the location, then spend the whole trip in Grab cars back and forth. This guide brings together 10 Chiang Mai hotels we've reviewed across every tier — from riverside luxury down to value boutiques and hostels. Every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Chiang Mai has no metro, but the city is compact — Grab and the red songthaews are convenient and cheap. From Chiang Mai Airport into town is about 15 minutes. The main areas in this guide: Old City — Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang, Tha Phae Gate, Sunday Walking Street · Nimman — cafes, One Nimman, MAYA, nightlife · Ping Riverside — quiet, resorts and boutiques, river views · Chang Khlan / Night Bazaar — night market, shopping · Mae Rim — hill valley outside town, nature resorts, around 30–40 minutes from the city.

entries.name: 137 Pillars House
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ping Riverside·Wat Gate · ~10 min to Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 2 Nawatgate Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.5 — 137 Pillars House is Chiang Mai's top-tier luxury stay, an all-suite property on a historic riverside plot in the Wat Gate area, built around an 1880 teak house. Every room is a suite starting at 70 sqm with a private balcony, and reviews repeatedly praise butler service that responds quickly without feeling intrusive. It's about a 10-minute walk to the Night Bazaar, yet once you're through the gate it falls quiet, as if you'd stepped out of the city.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a suite facing the main teak house directly, and check for packages that include breakfast at Palette, which reviews mention often.
pros: Every room is a suite from 70 sqm with a balcony — larger than most 5-star standard rooms
Butler service that responds quickly without feeling intrusive (per reviews)
Quiet riverside location, yet walkable to the Night Bazaar
An 1880 teak house, beautifully restored, with a genuine story
cons: Highest price in this guide — best for a special-occasion trip
Quiet Wat Gate area means you'll always need a car to reach town

entries.name: Akyra Manor Chiang Mai
entries.addr: 22/2 Nimmana Haeminda Rd Soi 9, Su Thep, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Akyra Manor is an all-suite design boutique in the heart of Nimman, a Small Luxury Hotels of the World member, scoring 9.3 from 426 reviews. What reviews mention most is the rooftop infinity pool and RISE Bar with city views, plus the outdoor bathtub on the balcony of every room. With just 30 suites it feels personal, and the Soi 9 location is a few minutes' walk to the cafes and MAYA.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Head up to the rooftop in the early evening before sunset, and request a higher-floor suite for an open view and quiet.
pros: Rooftop infinity pool and RISE Bar with city views (a frequent review highlight)
Every room is a suite with an outdoor bathtub on the balcony
Small property of 30 suites — personal service
Nimman Soi 9 location, walkable to cafes and MAYA
cons: Opened in 2015 — some rooms show their age in places
High-season prices rise and rooms fill fast as it's a small hotel

entries.name: U Nimman Chiang Mai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nimman Soi 1 · next to One Nimman
entries.addr: 1 Nimmanhaemin Road Lane 1, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If you want the best location in Nimman, U Nimman is the answer — it sits right next to One Nimman and is a short walk from MAYA, scoring 9.3 from 791 reviews. What reviews highlight most is the 24-hour stay system: whatever time you check in, your full day counts from that moment, and you can take breakfast anywhere, any time. It also has a rooftop pool with city views across its 147 rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a higher floor or an inward-facing room — it'll be quieter than the Nimman-street side on Friday and Saturday nights.
pros: Right next to One Nimman — the best location in the Nimman area
24-hour stay count makes your nightly rate go further
Take breakfast anywhere, any time
Rooftop pool with city views
cons: Lower-floor rooms catch Nimman nightlife noise on weekends
Standard Deluxe rooms are on the compact side

entries.name: Anantara Chiang Mai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ping Riverside·Chang Khlan · walk to Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 123-123/1 Charoen Prathet Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Anantara is a luxury riverside resort that's still walkable to town, scoring 9.2 from 203 reviews. Designed by architect Kerry Hill on the former British Consulate grounds, the 1921 House today serves as its restaurant and afternoon-tea venue. Deluxe rooms are a generous 50 sqm, and reviews say the river view is worth the upgrade. The Chang Khlan location is walkable to the Night Bazaar, yet you come back to riverside calm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a higher-floor Deluxe River View to escape street noise and get the full river view, and book afternoon tea at the 1921 House ahead.
pros: On the Ping River, walkable to the Night Bazaar
Restrained Kerry Hill design — unlike a typical resort
Riverside breakfast at Bodhi Terrace earns consistent praise (per reviews)
Roomy 50 sqm Deluxe rooms and the well-known Anantara Spa
cons: Bathrooms in Deluxe rooms feel small for the price (per reviews)
Street-facing rooms catch some road noise at times

entries.name: Stamps Backpackers
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.6 · 5,555 reviews · Best Social Hostel in Asia
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old City·Chaiyapoom Rd · walk to Tha Phae Gate
entries.addr: 1/11 Chaiyapoom Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Stamps Backpackers is the most-reviewed property in this guide — over 5,555 reviews at a 9.6 — and a Hoscars Best Social Hostel in Asia winner in 2024 and 2025. Its draw is the downstairs bar and nightly events for solo travellers who want to meet people; every pod bed has a privacy curtain, reading light, plug and a large locker. It's a walk to Tha Phae Gate and Wat Chiang Man.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's ages 18–35 only and genuinely social — if you want quiet sleep, pick elsewhere, but to meet people this is the best fit.
pros: Most reviewed in this guide at 5,555 · Best Social Hostel in Asia
Downstairs bar and nightly events — great for solo travellers
Pod beds with curtain, light, plug and large locker each
Old City location, walk to Tha Phae Gate and temples
cons: It's a social hostel with bar noise — not for those wanting quiet
Guests aged 18–35 only

entries.name: At Pingnakorn Riverside
entries.addr: 381 Charoen Rat Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: At Pingnakorn Riverside is the best-value riverside boutique in this guide, scoring 9.2 from 178 reviews. Reviews praise the roomy 42-sqm starting rooms at a from-฿1,400 rate — hard to find at this level — with a colonial-meets-Lanna design. There's an outdoor salt pool and the riverside Nakara restaurant, on the quiet east bank of the river in the Wat Gate area, still within reach of town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms are larger than the price suggests — ideal if you want a riverside feel without paying resort-luxury rates.
pros: Roomy 42-sqm starting rooms — excellent value at this price
Colonial-meets-Lanna design with character
Outdoor salt pool and the riverside Nakara restaurant
Quiet riverside location, still within reach of town
cons: Quiet Wat Gate area — you'll need a car to reach the main centres
It's a mid-size hotel, not an activity-packed resort

entries.name: Four Seasons Resort Chiang Mai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Rim · ~30–40 min from the city
entries.addr: 502 Moo 1, Mae Rim-Samoeng Old Road, Rim Tai, Mae Rim
entries.storyHtml: Four Seasons is a luxury resort in the Mae Rim hill valley with 3 MICHELIN Keys, scoring 9.1 from 128 reviews. What sets it apart is the working rice terraces across its 32-acre grounds, complete with a rice farm and resident buffalo. Pavilions and villas are scattered around the fields like a Lanna village, with an infinity pool over the valley and a Breakfast in the Rice Fields experience reviews call a highlight. The trade-off is its out-of-town location 30–40 minutes away, which places it here despite the high service level.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Best for those who plan to stay mainly within the resort, not for daily market-hopping · don't miss the Breakfast in the Rice Fields, which needs advance booking.
pros: Working rice terraces — northern countryside within a luxury setting
Infinity pool with valley views and the rice-fields breakfast
Personal service; staff remember guests by name (per reviews)
Holds 3 MICHELIN Keys, the top tier for accommodation
cons: Out of town, 30–40 minutes — a car ride every time you head in
On-site food and drink are pricey, with add-on activity fees (per reviews)

entries.name: Stay With Nimman
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Nimman · walk to One Nimman and MAYA
entries.addr: 8/8 Siri Mangkalajarn Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Stay With Nimman is a value design stay in the heart of Nimman with a large 1,562 reviews at 8.9. Its standout is two rooftop pools from a from-฿1,200 rate — excellent value for the Nimman area. The 133 modern rooms are within walking distance of One Nimman and MAYA, making it a fit for anyone who wants to be central in Nimman without paying boutique-luxury rates.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Head up to the rooftop pool in the early evening for the city view, and pick a room away from the main road for quiet.
pros: Two rooftop pools — great value from ฿1,200
Central Nimman location, walk to One Nimman and MAYA
A large 1,562 reviews, reflecting consistency
Modern design — ideal for budget travellers who want to be in Nimman
cons: It's a large property — service is less personal than a small boutique
Some rooms sit near the road in a lively area

entries.name: De Lanna Hotel
entries.badge: 🏮 Best value in the Old City
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old City · near Tha Phae Gate
entries.addr: 44 Intrawarorot Road, Sri Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: De Lanna is a Lanna boutique in the Old City at an affordable rate, scoring 8.7 from 786 reviews. The Lanna gabled-roof property hides in a tropical garden within the old walls, a few minutes' walk from Tha Phae Gate, the temples and the Sunday Walking Street. There's a garden pool and most rooms have a private balcony — a fit for anyone wanting a contemporary Thai feel and a central location on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a group or want more space? Look at the Deluxe or Suite, and visit the Old City temples early before the crowds.
pros: Central Old City location, walk to Tha Phae Gate and Walking Street
Lanna atmosphere in a tropical garden, with a pool
Good starting value for the Old City zone
Most rooms have a private balcony
cons: Superior rooms are compact — check the room type before booking
An older hotel (opened 2009) showing some wear in places

entries.name: Lanna Dusita Riverside Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ping Riverside·Pa Tan · ~15 min from Old City
entries.addr: 146 Paton Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Lanna Dusita is a Lanna boutique resort on the Ping River on a budget, scoring 8.7. Teak buildings sit around a leafy garden in the Pa Tan area, and from a ฿1,200 rate you still get a riverside-resort feel. Every room has a private balcony, there's a garden pool plus a kids' pool, and a free tuk-tuk shuttle into town helps with the location around 15 minutes from the Old City.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make full use of the free shuttle into town, and choose the Deluxe River View if you want a river view for a small premium.
pros: Riverside-resort feel from a ฿1,200 rate
Lanna teak buildings and a pool in a leafy garden
Every room has a private balcony; a kids' pool suits families
Free tuk-tuk shuttle into town
cons: Pa Tan location, around 15 minutes from the Old City
Few reviews so far (47) — it's a small resort

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Chiang Mai hotel for you

advice.head: On a budget, want the best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Stamps Backpackers ฿450, a social hostel in the Old City · or Lanna Dusita ฿1,200, a riverside Lanna teak resort with a free shuttle into town

advice.head: Solo traveller, want to meet people
advice.bodyHtml: → Stamps Backpackers ฿450, Best Social Hostel in Asia, with a downstairs bar and nightly events; ages 18–35 only

advice.head: Want to be in Nimman — cafes and shopping
advice.bodyHtml: → U Nimman ฿2,800, next to One Nimman · or Stay With Nimman ฿1,200, two rooftop pools at a value rate

advice.head: Special trip, luxury no limits
advice.bodyHtml: → 137 Pillars House ฿18,000, all-suite by the Ping River, scoring 9.5 · or Anantara Chiang Mai ฿8,500, a luxury riverside resort

advice.head: Want a nature stay out of town
advice.bodyHtml: → Four Seasons Resort ฿19,000, in the Mae Rim rice terraces with 3 MICHELIN Keys, best for those staying mainly within the resort

advice.head: Want temples, the Walking Street, the Old City
advice.bodyHtml: → De Lanna Hotel ฿1,400, a Lanna boutique walkable to Tha Phae Gate · or Stamps Backpackers ฿450 for a budget Old City base

advice.head: Want a quiet stay by the Ping River
advice.bodyHtml: → Anantara Chiang Mai Resort ฿8,500, riverside luxury walkable to town · or At Pingnakorn Riverside ฿1,400, a value riverside boutique

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are indicative starting rates from standard-room ranges and can change by date and season; always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking. Scores and highlights in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we did not stay personally. During festivals (Yi Peng/Loy Krathong in Nov, Songkran 13–15 Apr, New Year) prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book 1–2 months ahead. Chiang Mai has no metro — Grab and red songthaews are convenient, and the airport is about 15 minutes from town. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Chiang Mai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Old City suits temple-walking and the Walking Street (De Lanna, Stamps Backpackers) · Nimman suits cafes, shopping and nightlife (U Nimman, Akyra Manor, Stay With Nimman) · Ping Riverside suits quiet relaxation (137 Pillars House, Anantara, At Pingnakorn, Lanna Dusita) · Mae Rim suits a nature stay out of town (Four Seasons). All in-town areas are easily linked by Grab.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chiang Mai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels and budget stays start around ฿450–1,400 a night · boutiques and 4-star around ฿2,800–4,500 · resorts and 5-star luxury by the river or in the rice fields from ฿8,500–19,000+. All prices here are indicative starting rates from standard rooms; during festivals (Loy Krathong/Yi Peng in Nov, Songkran, New Year) they can run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chiang Mai hotel?
faq.a: For normal weekdays, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough. But during Yi Peng/Loy Krathong (November), Songkran (13–15 April) and New Year, good rooms fill fast — book 1–2 months ahead or more, especially for riverside and Old City hotels.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Chiang Mai hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so it's best to compare all 3 before booking. Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links — it can save several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay in the Old City or Nimman?
faq.a: The Old City suits trips focused on temples, history and the Walking Street, where you can walk everywhere — but it has fewer modern cafes. Nimman suits cafe-goers, modern dining, shopping at One Nimman and MAYA, and nightlife — but it's farther from the Old City temples, a 10–15 minute Grab ride away. On a longer trip, try staying in both.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get from Chiang Mai Airport into town?
faq.a: Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) is very close to town — about 15 minutes by car to the Old City or Nimman. A Grab from the airport is easiest, or use an airport taxi. Many hotels offer transfers (some free) — ask when you book. For Four Seasons in Mae Rim, it's about 35 minutes from the airport.
